subject: W4-A Task 1 canonical reservation lifecycle trace and first failing boundary
evidenceLevel: source code analysis and disposable PostgreSQL schema trace

redResult.case: canonical reservation committed under W3 is immutable historical truth, but canonical reservations currently have no authorized lifecycle/cancellation authority and no authorized booked-inventory release path
redResult.scope: disposable PostgreSQL with migrations 001-006, 036, 041, 049-054. Confirms that W3 canonical reservations are strictly immutable under trigger canonical_reservations_immutable; direct in-place UPDATE is rejected; and zero canonical lifecycle tables or cancellation request procedures exist in PostgreSQL.

sourceTracedRouteEvidence.guestCancellationRoute: server.ts:16165 (PUT /api/user/bookings/:id/cancel) updates legacy bookings table status='cancelled'. It has no relation to canonical_reservations or inventory_days.
sourceTracedRouteEvidence.hostStatusRoute: server.ts:15074 (PUT /api/host/reservations/:id/status) updates legacy bookings status without reaching canonical reservation state.
sourceTracedRouteEvidence.guestBookingsView: server.ts:16097 (GET /api/user/bookings) queries unallocated legacy bookings table; canonical reservations remain unprojected to guests.
sourceTracedRouteEvidence.clientCommandContainment: lib/reservationCommands.ts:30 contains single-flight session-checked invocation of legacy endpoints.

w3AllocationVsW4Lifecycle.w3AllocationState: canonical_reservations.status = 'INVENTORY_COMMITTED' is immutable physical room allocation truth (proves reservation exists and inventory was committed). It is not a mutable lifecycle state.
w3AllocationVsW4Lifecycle.w4InitialLifecycle: ACTIVE (derived from the existence of a valid canonical reservation in W3).

projectedStateModel.namingRule: State names represent lifecycle progression only; actor identity, reason, and origin are strictly separate dimensions.

smallestW4ASlice.lifecycleEventLedger: canonical_reservation_events append-only table recording lifecycle events for canonical_reservations(id).
smallestW4ASlice.commandReceiptLedger: canonical_reservation_lifecycle_commands table providing idempotent replay recovery.
smallestW4ASlice.currentLifecycleProjection: compact projection deriving current lifecycle state (initial: ACTIVE; transition: CANCELLATION_REQUESTED).
smallestW4ASlice.transitionSupported: CANCELLATION_REQUESTED recording only; completed cancellation is deferred to W4-B.

separatedDimensions.actor: actor_principal (e.g. user:10, staff:90) and actor_kind (GUEST, HOST, STAFF, EXTERNAL_CHANNEL)

deferredBoundaries.inventoryRelease: W4-B authority: modifying inventory_days.booked_units is deferred until cancellation completion contract is defined.
deferredBoundaries.genericModification: W4-C authority: date/room/rate modifications are deferred because they alter inventory, commercial totals, and payments.
deferredBoundaries.refundExecution: W4-D authority: payment ledger adjustments and provider refund requests are deferred to separate payment/refund authority.

commandIdempotencyInvariants: A. same command_id + same semantic request -> return existing lifecycle event and receipt
B. same command_id + changed semantics -> command conflict exception
C. concurrent identical lifecycle commands -> exactly one event inserted, one replayed receipt
D. concurrent different commands attempting the same lifecycle transition -> exactly one succeeds, second detects conflict or terminal state
E. W4-A must not create inventory or refund side effects
F. future W4-B inventory release must maintain a separate durable idempotency fence to prevent double-release of booked inventory

separationOfAuthorities.reservationLifecycle: Authority A: Contractual agreement state (ACTIVE -> CANCELLATION_REQUESTED).
separationOfAuthorities.inventoryConsequence: Authority B: Physical capacity in inventory_days. Separate authority; lifecycle request does not release inventory.
separationOfAuthorities.refundConsequence: Authority C: Payment refund tracking and execution. Separate authority; lifecycle request does not trigger or complete refund.

founderLegalCommercialGates: refund entitlement, eligibility and payable amounts
host cancellation consequences and compensation rules
no-show policy and payout forfeiture terms
conclusion: W3 canonical reservation finalization is immutable historical truth. Canonical reservations currently have no authorized lifecycle/cancellation authority and no authorized booked-inventory release path. The smallest W4-A slice introduces an append-only lifecycle event ledger and command idempotency ledger supporting CANCELLATION_REQUESTED with separated actor, reason, and origin dimensions, while deferring inventory release (W4-B), generic modification (W4-C), and refund execution (W4-D).
limitations: No runtime implementation, no canonical integration, no live money movement, no external APIs contacted. This is intentional red diagnostic and trace evidence for W4-A Task 1.
